articleBody:
Before ordering basement flooring, you must verify that the concrete foundation is completely prepared. Skipping slab assessment is the primary reason floating floors buckle and glued products peel.

Basement Slab Prep Checklist
- [ ] 24-hour polyethylene moisture test — Taping clear plastic sheets to the slab reveals hidden ground moisture if condensation or damp concrete appears beneath.
- [ ] Sump pump and perimeter drain inspection — Confirm mechanical water-relief systems are operating properly so rising water tables do not flood new underlayments.
- [ ] Exterior gutter and downspout check — Directing exterior roof runoff away from foundation walls prevents hydrostatic pressure from forcing water through the floor.
- [ ] Visual crack and spall audit — Map out all stress fractures, hollow spots, and crumbling aggregate that need hydraulic cement or structural epoxy patching.
- [ ] Concrete leveling survey — Place a six-foot straightedge across the slab to identify low dips or high humps exceeding manufacturer flatness tolerances.
- [ ] Chemical and residue sweep — Remove old carpet adhesives, paint drips, and drywall mud that can prevent moisture barriers or primers from bonding.
- [ ] Material acclimation staging — Store flooring boxes flat in the conditioned basement space for the manufacturer-recommended duration before opening packages.

How to Use This Checklist
Walk through these steps well ahead of your installation date. If moisture tests fail, you find extensive cracking, or your slab requires self-leveling underlayment, call HH Remodeling LLC at 303-505-0866 for a professional assessment.
